newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-HAEGGMAN AND CURRY SHOW WAY WITH RECORD ROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HAEGGMAN AND CURRY SHOW WAY WITH RECORD ROUNDS.

text.p: Joakim Haeggman of Sweden fired a course-record eight-under-par 63 early in the day which Englishman Paul Curry matched in the twilight for a share of the first round lead in the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Wednesday.

They beat the old record of 65 set by Jean Van de Velde in the inaugural event last year and left a clutch of international stars trailing in their wake on the 7,050-yard course beside the famous Scottish lake.

Haeggman, a Ryder Cup player in 1993, owed his score to his play on the greens where he needed just 27 putts, the first time he has got by with less than 33 since the first round of the British PGA Championship late in May.

"I was a little angry today after six holes because I was two under and I felt I could be four or five under. But I turned it around," said the Swede, who sustained a dislocated shoulder playing ice hockey late in 1994 which still hurts him.
He had nine birdies and an eagle against three bogeys, his eagle coming at the long 13th where he hit a brilliant three-wood second shot to five feet and holed the putt.
Curry, who shot a 60 in the 1992 Scottish Open at Gleneagles, disclosed that he had a back problem -- a prolapsed disc -- late last year that briefly threatened his career.
It has cleared up but he has missed eight cuts in 11 events this year.
"But five of them were by one stroke. I have not played that badly," he said.
He had eight birdies, six on the front nine and five in a row from the sixth.
Three came on putts of 45, 30 and 25 feet, another after a 181-yard six-iron that stopped two inches short of the cup at the seventh.
Tom Lehman, who will defend his British Open title next week at Royal Troon, began his warm-up impressively with a six-under-par 65, also compiled in the morning calm, to hold third place.
"How can you not be happy with a day like today. The weather was phenomenal, the golf course is perfect and I played well. It's just A-plus," Lehman said.
Fellow-American Glen Day held fourth place after a 66 while world number 10 Nick Faldo was in a group on four under with his 67.
The other big names were strung out behind, world number two Greg Norman sharing 10th place on 68.
Colin Montgomerie, Sunday's winner of the Irish Open, compiled a 69 and said he had trouble reading the putts.
Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal and U.S. Open champion Ernie Els were on 70, Ian Woosnam shot 72 and Bernhard Langer 73.
But the woes of Olazabal's compatriot, Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros, continued as he soared to a 79 after a nine-over-par back nine of 44.
Only two players, one an amateur, in the 153-man field did worse and the fading Spanish star looks almost certain to miss his 10th cut in 12 events this year.
